questions.question: A hundredths grid is made of 100 equal squares, and the whole grid stands for 1 whole. Exactly half of one square is shaded, which is ½% of the grid. Written as a decimal, ½% equals
questions.explain: Percent means hundredths, so ½% is half of one hundredth: 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. The common trap is 0.5, which reads ½% as just the fraction ½ and forgets the percent sign.

questions.question: Two hundredths grids sit side by side, each made of 100 equal squares, and one full grid stands for 1 whole. All 100 squares of the first grid are shaded and 22 squares of the second grid are shaded, which is 122%. Written as a decimal, 122% equals
questions.explain: 122% means 122 hundredths, so divide by 100: 122 ÷ 100 = 1.22, a number greater than 1 because more than one whole grid is shaded. The trap is 0.122, which moves the decimal point three places instead of two.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is made of 100 equal squares and stands for 1 whole. Three whole squares are shaded, and one quarter of a fourth square is shaded, which is 3.25% of the grid. Written as a decimal, 3.25% equals
questions.explain: To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100, which moves the decimal point two places left: 3.25% = 0.0325. The trap is 0.325, which moves the point only one place.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is made of 100 equal squares and stands for 1 whole. One quarter of a single square is shaded, which is ¼% of the grid. Written as a fraction of the whole grid in lowest terms, ¼% equals
questions.explain: ¼% is 0.25 out of 100, and multiplying the top and bottom of 0.25/100 by 4 clears the decimal to give 1/400. The trap is 1/4, which treats ¼% as if it were the plain fraction ¼.

questions.question: Which decimal is equal to ¾%?
questions.explain: First change the fraction to a decimal, ¾ = 0.75, then divide by 100 because percent means hundredths: 0.0075. The trap is 0.75, which drops the percent sign partway through.

questions.question: A savings account at a credit union in Nanaimo pays 0.4% interest each year. Written as a fraction in lowest terms, 0.4% equals
questions.explain: 0.4% means 0.4 out of 100, so 0.4/100 = 4/1000 = 1/250. The trap is 2/5, which is just 0.4 written as a fraction without ever dividing by 100.

questions.question: This year a Vancouver bus route carried 145% of the riders it carried last year. Written as a decimal, 145% equals
questions.explain: Divide by 100 to undo the percent: 145 ÷ 100 = 1.45, and any percent above 100% must give a decimal greater than 1. The trap is 0.145, which shifts the decimal point three places instead of two.

questions.question: Amara wants to write 6½% as a decimal. Which plan gives the correct decimal?
options: Write 6½% as 6.5, then move one place left to get 0.65
Write 6½% as 6.5%, then divide by 10 to get 0.65
Write 6½% as 6 plus one half, so the decimal is 6.5
Write 6½% as 6.5%, then divide by 100 to get 0.065
questions.explain: Change the fraction part to a decimal first (6½% = 6.5%), then divide by 100 because percent means hundredths, giving 0.065. The trap is dividing by 10, which shifts the point only one place.

questions.question: Two bike shops in Victoria add a service fee to a repair bill. Shop A charges a fee of 1¼% of the bill and Shop B charges a fee of 0.5% of the bill. Which choice writes both fees as decimals and names the larger fee?
options: 0.0125 and 0.005; Shop A's fee is larger
0.125 and 0.05; Shop A's fee is larger
1.25 and 0.5; Shop A's fee is larger
0.00125 and 0.0005; Shop B's fee is larger
questions.explain: 1¼% = 1.25% = 0.0125 and 0.5% = 0.005, so Shop A charges more. The trap is writing 1.25 and 0.5, which keeps the numbers as they look and forgets that percent means hundredths.

questions.question: Leah's sunflower was 40 cm tall in June. In July its height was 135% of its June height. Which choice writes 135% as a decimal and gives the July height?
options: 0.135; the plant is 5.4 cm tall
1.35; the plant is 54 cm tall
13.5; the plant is 540 cm tall
1.035; the plant is 41.4 cm tall
questions.explain: 135% = 135 ÷ 100 = 1.35, and then 1.35 × 40 = 54 cm. The trap is 0.135, which shifts the decimal three places and would make the sunflower shrink even though 135% is more than the whole.

questions.question: Jordan wrote ¼% = 0.25 on a quiz. Which choice explains the work and gives the correct decimal?
options: 0.25 is correct, because ¼% means one quarter of 1 whole
Only one place was shifted instead of two; ¼% = 0.025
¼ became 0.25 but the percent was dropped; ¼% = 0.0025
Three places were shifted instead of two; ¼% = 0.00025
questions.explain: Changing ¼ to 0.25 is only the first step, because ¼% still means 0.25 hundredths, so divide by 100 to get 0.0025. The trap is stopping at 0.25, as though ¼% and ¼ were the same amount.

questions.question: A survey of 4000 students in Surrey found that 0.25% of them chose curling as their favourite winter sport. Which choice writes 0.25% as a decimal and gives the number of students?
options: 0.25; 1000 students chose curling
0.00025; 1 student chose curling
0.025; 100 students chose curling
0.0025; 10 students chose curling
questions.explain: 0.25% = 0.25 ÷ 100 = 0.0025, and 0.0025 × 4000 = 10 students. The trap is using 0.25 and getting 1000, which ignores the percent sign and turns a tiny percent into a quarter of the school.
